findings.title: Audit log list and export are not org-scoped by default
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/audit.ts:22 — router.use(requireAuth, requireOrgAccess, requireAdmin) now mounts the org gate (the finding's root cause)
apps/api/src/routes/audit.ts:34-35 — list applies applyRequestedOrg(...) then the mandatory applyOrgScope(query, 'organization_id', scope) so a single-org admin can never widen scope
apps/api/src/routes/audit.ts:77-78 — /export applies the same mandatory predicates before sendExportResponse
apps/api/src/routes/audit.ts:125,171 — /impersonation and /impersonation/export are gated on resolveAdminTenantScope().allTenants (is_super_admin + cross-tenant role), 403 otherwise
apps/api/src/lib/admin-scope.ts:70-99 — applyOrgScope fails closed to NO_ORG_MATCH and applyRequestedOrg 403s a requested org outside the caller's approved set
apps/api/src/__tests__/audit.test.ts — route suite exists at this commit
findings.impact: Previously any single-org admin could read every tenant's audit trail. Now list/export are pinned to the caller's approved orgs and platform-wide review surfaces require a genuine cross-tenant admin.
findings.recommendation: None required; keep the applyOrgScope pattern as the reference for other tenant tables and add a route-level regression test asserting an org B ?organization_id is 403 for an org A admin.

findings.title: Platform dashboards expose all-tenant aggregates to any single-org admin
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/dashboard.ts:16-50 — /summary resolves resolveAdminTenantScope and wraps every count (organizations, tickets, projects, documents, pending memberships) in applyOrgScope
apps/api/src/routes/business-os.ts:41-94 — /summary scopes orgs/tickets/projects/documents/approvals via applyOrgScope and restricts profile counts to scoped member ids (business-os.ts:24-33)
apps/api/src/routes/business-os.ts:148-155,172-179,196-201 — approvals-overdue, recent-activity and org-health apply the mandatory org predicate
apps/api/src/routes/business-os.ts:264-266 — business_os_snapshots is served only when scope.allTenants (empty list otherwise)
apps/api/src/lib/admin-scope.ts:55-57 — allTenants requires is_super_admin AND a cross-tenant role key, so a plain tenant admin is scoped
findings.impact: Previously any tenant admin saw platform-wide counts and recent audit activity. Now a single-org admin only sees their own tenant(s); only a genuine cross-tenant admin sees platform aggregates.
findings.recommendation: None required; consider auditing the allTenants read path (the metric/impersonation trail) so a platform-wide dashboard read is visible in the review surface.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: dashboard.ts and business-os.ts use resolveAdminTenantScope + applyOrgScope on every aggregate; MT-P1-002 regression closed.

findings.title: Public file-request upload authorizes with a permission unioned across all orgs
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/file-requests.ts:109-117 — POST /public/:token/upload no longer calls requirePermission; the token row is the authorization capability and the comment records the fix (FILE-P1-001 / MT-P1-003)
apps/api/src/routes/file-requests.ts:122-149 — the file_requests row is loaded by token and status/expiry/max-files/MIME/size are all validated against the row
apps/api/src/routes/file-requests.ts:156 — storagePath is derived from data.organization_id (never caller input): `${data.organization_id}/requests/${data.token}/...`
apps/api/src/routes/file-requests.ts:184-190 — claim_file_request_slot is bound to p_organization_id from the row, so a slot cannot be claimed across orgs
apps/api/src/routes/file-requests.ts:210-218 — file_request_uploads row is written with organization_id from the request row
apps/api/src/routes/file-requests.ts:408 — the authenticated create path also pins storagePath to parsed.organizationId (which requireOrgAccess checked)
findings.impact: Previously a user granted file-requests:create in org A could upload into org B's request folder. Uploads are now bound to the token's owning org end to end (path, slot claim, DB row).
findings.recommendation: None required; add a regression test that an org A JWT cannot consume an org B token's quota (or is rejected) and that the stored path always starts with the request row's org id.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: token-bound org derivation and claim RPC present; MT-P1-003 regression closed.

findings.title: Admin global search lists all organizations and can fall through unscoped
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/search.ts:77-79 — requestedOrgId comes from req.orgScope only when explicit; scopedOrgIds falls back to the caller's approved memberships

apps/api/src/routes/search.ts:118-163 — tickets/projects/documents/organizations all get .in('organization_id', scopedOrgIds.length ? scopedOrgIds : ['__no_match__']) unless a genuine all-tenants admin (is_super_admin + cross-tenant role, search.ts:55-70) is searching without an explicit org
apps/api/src/routes/search.ts:91-111 — user search is limited to approved members of scopedOrgIds and fails closed on an empty set
apps/api/src/routes/search.ts:193-211 — the all-tenants path is audited (metadata.allTenants)
apps/api/src/__tests__/search-tenant-scope.test.ts:136-225 — regression tests for fail-closed, explicit-org narrowing and audited all-tenants
findings.impact: Previously any admin could enumerate all tenants via the organizations search and could fall through unscoped. Now a single-org admin is confined to their orgs and an empty scope returns no rows.
findings.recommendation: None required; keep the search-tenant-scope suite as the template for other cross-tenant search surfaces.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: scoped org ids + fail-closed sentinel + audited allTenants path; MT-P2-001 regression closed.

findings.title: By-id org filters are conditional, so they fail open if the org gate is not reached
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/findings.ts:80-82,108-110,137-139 — `if (orgId) query = query.eq("organization_id", orgId)` remains the idiom on list/stats/by-id reads
apps/api/src/routes/qbr.ts:25-28,45-50,214-219,240-245 — qbr_reports reads/writes filter by req.query.organization_id only if present
apps/api/src/routes/documents.ts:218-219,248-250 — documents list/by-id keep the conditional predicate (mutations use loadOwned, reads do not)
apps/api/src/routes/tickets.ts:104-113 — tickets list/by-id conditional on req.query.organization_id
apps/api/src/middleware/org-access.ts:210-211,226-227 — the safety of the conditional form depends on requireOrgAccess injecting organization_id and setting req.orgId

apps/api/src/__tests__/tenant-scoping-guard.test.ts:46-111 — the QW-3 static guard allowlists ~58 route files (including findings, approvals, proposals, api-keys, tickets) so new unscoped :param handlers there are not caught
apps/api/src/lib/admin-scope.ts:70-99 — the mandatory-predicate fix pattern (applyOrgScope/applyRequestedOrg) has been adopted only on exports/dashboard/audit so far

apps/api/src/routes/client-portal.ts:113,137 — concrete residual: requireAdmin runs before requireOrgAccess, so the org-pinned admin check in middleware/admin.ts:49-58 is skipped (see separate finding)
findings.impact: Tenant scoping on by-id/list reads remains an emergent property of middleware ordering + query injection rather than a local invariant; one route mounted without requireOrgAccess (or one middleware reorder) fails open against the service-role client. No live exploit was reproduced at this commit for ordinary tenant users, but the footgun is still present and the guard test does not cover the allowlisted modules.
findings.recommendation: Migrate conditional `if (orgId)` reads to the mandatory predicate helper (applyOrgScope/applyRequestedOrg) or a tenantQuery(req, table) helper that throws when a non-platform caller has no resolved org; then shrink the KNOWN_UNSCOPED allowlist to only genuinely global/user-scoped modules.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: partial progress — exports/audit/dashboard now use mandatory predicates and loadOwned covers many mutations, but the conditional by-id pattern is still dominant across 11+ route files and the static guard allowlists them; residual documented above.

findings.title: Storage writer path and RLS org-derivation disagree (`orgs/<uuid>/` vs `<uuid>/`)
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/documents.ts:352 — storagePath is now `${organizationId}/${Date.now()}-${safeName}` (raw org UUID first, no `orgs/` prefix)
apps/api/src/routes/file-requests.ts:156 — public upload path is `${data.organization_id}/requests/${data.token}/...`
apps/api/src/routes/file-requests.ts:408 — create path is `${parsed.organizationId}/requests/${token}`
supabase/migrations/5302026_supabase_consolidated_fresh_bootstrap_20260529.corrected.v3.sql:799-825 — storage_path_org_id regex requires `^<uuid>(/|$)`
supabase/migrations/5302026_..._v3.sql:2326-2337,2341-2353 — documents bucket insert/update policies call storage_path_org_id(name) and require it non-null
apps/api/src/routes/documents.ts:349-356 — comment records the alignment (MT-P2-003 / FILE-P1-002)
findings.impact: Writer and policy now agree, so RLS on the documents bucket can derive the tenant for every API-written object; the earlier mismatch (uploads denied or orphaned under RLS) is closed.
findings.recommendation: None required; add a unit test asserting storage_path_org_id('<uuid>/x') returns the UUID and that every writer path starts with the org UUID.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: documents and file-requests writers emit <orgId>/... matching the storage_path_org_id contract and the bucket policies; MT-P2-003 regression closed.

findings.title: Realtime/SSE notification channel is scoped by user only, with no org assertion
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/notifications.ts:36-44 — notificationInScope(row, userId, scopedOrgId) drops rows whose user_id or organization_id do not match the resolved scope
apps/api/src/routes/notifications.ts:59,120,135 — scopedOrgId = req.orgId, asserted on both INSERT and UPDATE realtime handlers
apps/api/src/routes/notifications.ts:147-156 — the initial unread query is additionally filtered by organization_id when an org is resolved
apps/api/src/__tests__/notifications-sse-scope.test.ts:17-37 — unit tests cover same-org accept, cross-org drop, cross-user drop and the un-pinned platform-admin case
git show 1fb034bd — PR #145 implemented the assertion; notifications.ts has no later commits at 8d299b8d
findings.impact: The SSE stream no longer delivers notification rows outside the caller's resolved org, closing the cross-org stream leak identified in MT-P2-004.
findings.recommendation: None required; optionally also scope the REST list endpoints (GET /notifications, /unread-count) to the resolved org for consistency with the stream (currently user-scoped only — see the notification-recipient finding).
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: notificationInScope + scoped initial query present and unit-tested; PR #145 (1fb034bd) is the tip change to notifications.ts — MT-P2-004 regression closed.

findings.title: Platform-admin cross-tenant access is role-key based, broad, and unalerted
evidence: apps/api/src/lib/roles.ts:27 — CROSS_TENANT_KEYS = ['super_admin','admin']; any approved membership holding `admin` anywhere is cross-tenant
apps/api/src/middleware/org-access.ts:43-60,111-125 — checkOrgAccess/resolveDefaultOrgId grant access to any org when the caller holds a cross-tenant key, flagged platformAdmin+impersonation
apps/api/src/services/impersonation.ts:28-47 — cross-tenant access is written to impersonation_log and increments portal_impersonation_events_total (metrics.ts:253-255)
infra/digitalocean/prometheus.rules.yml:45-56 — alert 'Elevated cross-tenant (impersonation) access volume' (>0.5/s over 10m) with a review pointer to GET /api/v1/audit/impersonation
apps/api/src/routes/audit.ts:122-153 — allTenants-only impersonation review/export endpoints exist

apps/api/src/middleware/org-access.ts:52,197 and apps/api/src/lib/tenant.ts:46 — logImpersonation is fire-and-forget (`void`), so a failed log write does not block the access and can leave a silent trail gap

apps/api/src/middleware/admin.ts:49-58 — the org-pinned admin check that would restrict a plain `admin` to super_admin-only cross-tenant on admin routes is order-dependent (bypassed in client-portal.ts:113,137)
findings.impact: Cross-tenant access by a tenant-level `admin` remains broad (any requireOrgAccess-gated route) and is now logged, metered and volume-alerted; however the trail is best-effort (fire-and-forget), a single cross-tenant read does not alert, and the intended super_admin-only tightening for admin routes is inconsistently enforced.
findings.recommendation: Make impersonation_log writes awaited/queued-durable for cross-tenant requests (or fail closed on log failure), add a low-volume alert for first-seen actor→org pairs, and decide one policy for `admin` cross-tenant reach (either split the role keys or make requireAdmin ordering irrelevant by asserting the pinned org in requireOrgAccess).
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: alerting/logging now present (impersonation_log + metric + Prometheus rule + review endpoint), addressing the 'unalerted' part; the role-key breadth and fire-and-forget trail gap remain, so residual documented.

findings.title: Platform-wide report generators run as service role with no tenant guard on scope inputs
evidence: apps/worker/src/tasks/retention.ts:92-96 — config = { ...DEFAULT_CONFIG, ...(payload as Partial<RetentionConfig>) } — a caller-supplied payload still overrides retention windows
apps/worker/src/tasks/retention.ts:104-116 — only the numeric sanity guard (positive days) was added; there is no tenant/authorization guard on the payload
apps/worker/src/tasks/retention.ts:60-88 — purgeInBatches deletes audit_logs/notifications globally with the service-role client
apps/worker/src/tasks/module-tasks.ts:992-1124 — qbrScheduledGenerate runs as service role across every org's qbr_reports (per-row organization_id scoping is correct)
apps/worker/src/tasks/module-tasks.ts:1287-1350 — businessOsSnapshot computes org-wide metrics for all orgs as service role

apps/api/src/lib/task-producer.ts:76-104 — enqueueTask accepts any { taskType, payload } with no tenant validation; current call sites are internal (notify.ts:215, webhook-dispatcher.ts:147, webhook-management.ts:196)
findings.impact: No user-facing trigger was found, so the risk stays latent; but any future path that lets a lower-trust caller influence a queue payload can drive global service-role report/purge tasks with no tenant check. The retention batching/cap guard added since the original finding improves safety against misconfiguration, not against scope widening.
findings.recommendation: Validate task payloads at the registry boundary (reject org-scoped payload fields for global tasks; require and verify an org for tenant tasks), keep destructive tasks scheduled-only, and add a test that an unknown/widening payload is rejected.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: no tenant guard was added; retention still merges caller payload over defaults (retention.ts:92-96) and qbr/snapshot jobs remain service-role global. No user-facing enqueue path found today.

findings.title: No automated cross-tenant isolation regression suite for application-layer scoping
evidence: apps/api/src/__tests__/tenant-scoping-guard.test.ts:140-191 — QW-3 static guard walks every route file for unscoped :param handlers, but the KNOWN_UNSCOPED allowlist (lines 46-111, ~58 entries) covers most tenant modules so violations there are not caught
apps/api/src/__tests__/search-tenant-scope.test.ts — behavioral cross-tenant regression tests for search (fail-closed, explicit-org narrowing)
apps/api/src/__tests__/store-tenant-isolation.test.ts — single-org vs cross-tenant admin behavior for store rows
apps/api/src/__tests__/notifications-sse-scope.test.ts — SSE org assertion tests
apps/api/src/__tests__/middleware-org-access.test.ts (730 lines) and apps/api/src/__tests__/tenant.test.ts — middleware/helper behavior
No per-route suite was found that authenticates as org A and asserts 404/403 for org B ids across the route tree (e.g. tickets, documents, approvals, findings, qbr)
findings.impact: The core isolation property is now encoded for several modules and a static guard exists, but the guard's stale allowlist (including files that already use loadOwned) means new IDOR-class handlers in those files pass CI. The end-to-end 'no route returns another tenant's object' property is still not systematically tested.
findings.recommendation: Add a parameterized org A→org B suite per route module (known org B ids return 403/404; list endpoints without an explicit org return only org A rows), and shrink KNOWN_UNSCOPED to genuinely global/user-scoped modules so the guard has teeth.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: cross-tenant tests now exist for search/store/SSE plus a static guard (partial fix), but the guard allowlist is stale/broad and no per-route org A→B behavioral suite exists; residual documented.

findings.title: Response cache keys omit the caller's tenant scope, so all-tenant responses can be served to single-org members
evidence: apps/api/src/middleware/cache.ts:154-168 — buildCacheKey suffixes the key with `:org=<req.orgId>` for any request with a resolved org; the caller's user id and membership set are only used when orgId is absent

apps/api/src/middleware/org-access.ts:210-211,226-227 — for tenant users requireOrgAccess injects organization_id and sets req.orgId to the active/default org, so every member of an org shares the same cache key

apps/api/src/routes/organizations.ts:169-182 — GET /organizations returns rows for the caller's resolved scope: a super_admin+cross-tenant role (resolveAdminTenantScope allTenants) gets ALL orgs, while a member gets only their orgs — same cache key `...:org=<activeOrg>` for both
apps/api/src/routes/organizations.ts:153 — the route is cached with responseCacheNoRenew(60)
apps/api/src/routes/dashboard.ts:16,21-50 — cached /summary returns platform-wide counts for allTenants and org-scoped counts otherwise, keyed by org only
apps/api/src/routes/business-os.ts:35-143,193-257 — cached /summary, /org-health and /recent-activity vary with the resolved scope (org list, per-org health, audit rows) but share the org-only key
apps/api/src/lib/admin-scope.ts:55-57 — scope (allTenants, orgIds) is derived per caller from their memberships, i.e. the response is caller-dependent while the key is not
findings.impact: Within the TTL (30-60s), a response produced for a cross-tenant/platform admin (all-tenant org list, platform-wide counts, other orgs' names/status/plans/aggregates) can be served to a different user whose active org matches the key — e.g. any regular member of that org. Two single-org admins with different membership sets also collide. This is a cross-tenant metadata/aggregate disclosure driven purely by cache-key construction.
findings.recommendation: Include the resolved scope in the cache key (e.g. hash of orgScope.allTenants + sorted scope.orgIds, or scope.impersonation) and never serve an allTenants response from an org-keyed entry; add a unit test that two callers with the same active org but different membership sets do not share a cache entry.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; static reasoning only (no server run) — the HIT path is unambiguous: key depends on req.orgId, response depends on resolveAdminTenantScope(req).

findings.title: Client-portal entitlement routes order requireAdmin before requireOrgAccess, bypassing the org-pinned admin check
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/client-portal.ts:113 — router.get('/entitlements', requireAdmin, requireOrgAccess, ...)
apps/api/src/routes/client-portal.ts:137 — router.put('/entitlements', requireAdmin, requireOrgAccess, ...)

apps/api/src/middleware/admin.ts:46-58 — the org-pinned tightening only fires when req.orgScope.explicit === true && req.orgId is set, which requireOrgAccess has not done yet at this point in the chain

apps/api/src/middleware/org-access.ts:234-247 — requireOrgAccess then grants the same request: a caller with a cross-tenant `admin` key in any org is allowed into the target org as platformAdmin+impersonation
apps/api/src/middleware/org-access.ts:22 — extractOrgId prefers the query/body organization_id, so the target org is caller-supplied
apps/api/src/routes/client-portal.ts:147-149 — the PUT upserts client_portal_entitlements for parsed.organizationId
Contrast: apps/api/src/routes/audit.ts:22 and apps/api/src/routes/bulk.ts:11 mount requireOrgAccess BEFORE requireAdmin, so the pinned check applies there
findings.impact: A tenant-level `admin` (not super_admin) can read and modify another tenant's client-portal module entitlements — an admin-only surface the requireAdmin tightening was written to protect (ADMIN-P1-001) — with only an audited impersonation row. Enforcement is chain-order dependent and contradicts the audit/bulk ordering.
findings.recommendation: Swap the order to requireOrgAccess, requireAdmin on both routes (or assert the pinned org inside the handlers), and add a test that a plain admin of org A receives 403 on org B entitlements while a super_admin succeeds.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; cross-checked requireAdmin semantics and all four orderings in the tree (audit/bulk correct; search/client-portal inverted, but search re-derives scope itself).

findings.title: Platform-wide store intake and analytics endpoints are readable by any tenant admin with no cross-tenant gate
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/store/quotes.ts:200-216 — GET /store/quote-requests: requireAuth, requireAdmin, no requireOrgAccess/applyOrgScope; returns every row (customer name/email/phone/notes) ordered by created_at
apps/api/src/routes/store/quotes.ts:217-232 — GET /store/leads: same shape, returns all scored leads with lead scores/bands
apps/api/src/routes/store/quotes.ts:350-390 — GET /store/proposal-drafts and PATCH /store/proposal-drafts/:id: all drafts, update by id, no tenant/scope predicate

supabase/migrations/5302114_store_conversion_modules.sql:6-17 and 5302115_store_v5_sales_ops.sql:6-28 — store_quote_requests, store_leads and store_proposal_drafts have NO organization_id column (global tables)

supabase/migrations/5302408_store_tenant_scoping.sql:43-52 — the sibling store_quotes table WAS given organization_id and org-scoped RLS, and routes/store/quotes.ts:165-197 explicitly gates global/other-tenant quotes on a genuine cross-tenant admin (MT-P0-005)

apps/api/src/routes/analytics.ts:64-91 — GET /api/v1/analytics and /summary: requireAuth, requireAdmin, no tenant scope; store_analytics_events is a global table (migration 5302106_store_analytics.sql:1-25) containing anonymous_id, ip_address and user_agent
apps/api/src/routes/business-os.ts:264-266 — the analogous platform-level table (business_os_snapshots) is gated on scope.allTenants, showing the intended pattern
findings.impact: Any tenant-level admin (or any `admin`-key holder) can read platform-wide store intake PII and the internal sales pipeline, and platform-wide analytics including visitor IPs — with no impersonation record and no allTenants check. The inconsistency with the fixed store_quotes/business_os paths makes the gap a live cross-tenant/privacy exposure rather than a design decision.
findings.recommendation: Gate these endpoints on resolveAdminTenantScope().allTenants (or add organization_id + org RLS and scope by it), or document them as platform-staff-only and move them under a platform-admin surface; add regression tests mirroring store-tenant-isolation.test.ts.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; store_quotes was fixed for this exact class (MT-P0-005) but the sibling intake/analytics endpoints were not.

findings.title: Admin notification create accepts an arbitrary recipient and org-less rows bypass the SSE scope assertion
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/notifications.ts:292-320 — POST /notifications (requireAdmin) accepts any userId and an optional organizationId, then calls createNotification with the caller-supplied values
apps/api/src/lib/notify.ts:90-105 — insertNotification writes user_id/organization_id exactly as given (organization_id null when omitted); no check that sender and recipient share an org
apps/api/src/routes/notifications.ts:194-218 — GET /notifications lists by user_id only (no org filter), so an org-less notification is still shown in the recipient's list
apps/api/src/routes/notifications.ts:36-44 — the SSE stream drops org-less rows when an org is resolved, so the same content is inconsistently visible via REST but not SSE
apps/api/src/routes/notifications.ts:236-260,370-392 — read/delete are correctly user-scoped
findings.impact: A tenant admin can inject an arbitrary title/body notification (e.g. a phishing-style prompt) into any user's notification list across tenant boundaries, and the resulting org-less row is inconsistently handled between REST and SSE. Low severity: admin-only, audited, no data read.
findings.recommendation: Require the recipient to share the caller's resolved org (assertSharesActiveOrg) or set organization_id = req.orgId on insert, and filter the REST list by the resolved org like the SSE stream does.
findings.note: new finding at 8d299b8d; the MT-P2-004 fix scoped the stream but the create path and REST list were left as-is.

report:
# Multi-Tenant Isolation Attack Simulation

## Audit Metadata

- Audit name: repo-deep-dive
- Run: `mainecybertech-20261011-0426-full-main-8d299b8`
- Repository: `/tmp/opencode/mct-audit-target` (MaineCyberTech portal monorepo)
- Branch: `main`
- Commit SHA: `8d299b8d` (short `8d299b8`)
- Generated at: 2026-10-11
- Auditor: automated domain subagent (prompt 25), static/read-only analysis
- Area code: MT
- Output path (pack): `_domains/25_multi_tenant_isolation_attack_simulation_body.md`
- Scope limitations:
  - **No execution.** No requests were sent; no database, Supabase project, Redis, or lab system was touched. All conclusions are static reasoning over source, migrations, tests, and docs.
  - Deployed `RLS_READS_ENABLED` / `RLS_WRITES_ENABLED` values are deployment secrets (`.github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:615-616`); "which modules are RLS-enforced in production" remains `Unknown`.
  - Dynamic confirmation of the cache-collision finding requires two API clients plus Redis; it is marked as static-only.
  - Prior-run continuity used the committed 20261002 corpus in-repo: `docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/20261002-0344-develop-6286137/25_multi_tenant_isolation_attack_simulation.md` plus this run's `follow_up_register.md`.

## Scope

Reviewed (static evidence):

- Tenant resolution and gates: `requireOrgAccess`, `requireOrgAccessByParam`, `requireAdmin`, `requirePermission`, `assertBodyOrgMatches`, `assertOrgScopeMatches`, `assertSharesActiveOrg`, `resolveAdminTenantScope`, `applyOrgScope`, `applyRequestedOrg`, `assertResourceOrg`, `loadOwned`.
- DB client selection: `getSupabaseAdmin`, `getSupabaseUser`, `getScopedClient`, RLS startup check.
- Every API route module (62 files) for by-id handlers, conditional vs mandatory org predicates, router middleware ordering, and routes registered before the org gate.
- Realtime/SSE (`routes/notifications.ts`), storage paths (`documents`, `file-requests`, `profiles`, `organizations`), exports (`csv.ts`), search (`search.ts`, `search-portal.ts`), cache keys (`middleware/cache.ts`), invitations (`memberships.ts`, `organizations.ts`), admin overrides (`users.ts`), platform-admin paths (`admin.ts`, `audit.ts`, `business-os.ts`, `roles.ts`, `analytics.ts`, `store/*`), webhooks, and worker jobs.
- RLS migrations: membership helpers, `storage_path_org_id`, `notifications`, `profiles`, `tickets` policies; `docs/RLS-coverage-matrix.md`.

Not reviewed here: UI rendering, billing reconciliation (29), notification delivery (30), search indexing internals (31), and the live RLS allow-list values (unknown, see Open Questions).

## Evidence Reviewed

## Executive Summary

The isolation posture has improved materially since the original MT report (`6286137`, 2026-10-02). All three former P1s are fixed and re-verified at `8d299b8d`: audit list/export are tenant-pinned (`applyOrgScope`/`applyRequestedOrg`), dashboard/business-os aggregates are scoped to the caller's approved orgs (platform-wide views require `is_super_admin` + a cross-tenant role), and the public file-request upload derives its org from the token row end to end. Search fails closed, storage paths match the `storage_path_org_id` RLS contract, and the SSE notification stream now asserts the resolved org (PR #145, unit-tested). The `loadOwned`/`assertResourceOrg` entity→org pattern covers most mutation paths, and a static "unscoped `:param`" guard plus four behavioral cross-tenant suites now exist.

Three residual gaps matter:

1. **Cache keys omit the resolved tenant scope** (`middleware/cache.ts:154-168`). Responses that vary with the caller's membership set — the organizations list, dashboard counts, business-os summaries/org-health — are cached under `:org=<activeOrg>` only. Within the 30-60s TTL, an all-tenant response produced for a cross-tenant/platform admin can be served to a regular member of that org, and two admins with different membership sets collide. This is the only new P1.
2. **Conditional `if (orgId)` by-id filters remain the dominant idiom** (findings, qbr, tickets, documents reads, and others) and are safe only because `requireOrgAccess` injects the org. The static guard allowlists ~58 files, so the footgun is not enforced. A concrete residual is `client-portal.ts:113,137`, where `requireAdmin` runs *before* `requireOrgAccess` and therefore skips the org-pinned admin check, letting a tenant `admin` read/write another tenant's entitlements (P2).
3. **Platform-wide admin surfaces are inconsistent.** `store/quotes.ts:200-232,350-390` and `analytics.ts:64-91` expose global intake PII, the sales pipeline, and visitor IP analytics to any tenant admin with no `allTenants` gate, while the analogous `store_quotes` and `business_os_snapshots` paths *are* gated (P2).

Cross-tenant platform-admin access is now logged (`impersonation_log`), metered and volume-alerted, but the log write is fire-and-forget and `admin` remains a blanket cross-tenant key (MT-P2-005 partially fixed). Background report/purge jobs still accept payload overrides with no tenant guard, though no user-facing enqueue path was found (MT-P2-006 still open, latent).

**Domain score: 4/5** — functional and now meaningfully hardened at the application layer, with a small number of concrete residuals and RLS still an opt-in backstop.

## Detailed Review

### Item: Tenant resolution and the conditional-filter contract

- Evidence: `apps/api/src/middleware/org-access.ts:177-325`; `apps/api/src/routes/findings.ts:80-82`; `apps/api/src/routes/qbr.ts:25-50`.
- What it does: resolves the org from query → body → `X-Active-Org` → cookie; verifies an approved membership; grants cross-tenant access to `admin`/`super_admin` keys (audited); injects `organization_id` into `req.query` and sets `req.orgId` when no explicit org was given.
- Current controls: injection + `assertBodyOrgMatches` + mandatory predicates on the hardened surfaces.
- Missing controls: by-id/list reads still use `if (orgId)` in many files; a route mounted without `requireOrgAccess` (or reordered middleware) fails open.
- Risks: MT-P2-002 residual; see the client-portal ordering finding.
- Recommended improvement: `tenantQuery(req, table)` helper that throws when a non-platform caller has no resolved org; shrink the static guard allowlist.

### Item: Platform-admin cross-tenant access (MT-P2-005)

- Evidence: `apps/api/src/lib/roles.ts:27`; `apps/api/src/services/impersonation.ts:28-47`; `apps/api/src/lib/metrics.ts:253-255`; `infra/digitalocean/prometheus.rules.yml:45-56`; `apps/api/src/routes/audit.ts:122-153`.
- What it does: any approved membership with `admin`/`super_admin` may enter any tenant; each entry writes `impersonation_log` (reason, IP, UA) and increments a metric; a Prometheus rule alerts above 0.5 events/s and points at the review endpoint.
- Missing controls: log write is `void` (best-effort); volume threshold means a single cross-tenant read never alerts; `admin` vs `super_admin` reach is inconsistent across gates (client-portal finding).
- Recommended improvement: durable/queued audit writes, first-seen actor→org alert, and one explicit policy for `admin` cross-tenant reach.

### Item: Store intake and analytics (new)

- Evidence: `apps/api/src/routes/store/quotes.ts:200-232,350-390`; `apps/api/src/routes/analytics.ts:64-91`; `supabase/migrations/5302114_store_conversion_modules.sql:6-17`; `supabase/migrations/5302408_store_tenant_scoping.sql:43-52`; `apps/api/src/routes/business-os.ts:264-266`.
- What it does: exposes global `store_quote_requests` (customer PII), `store_leads`, `store_proposal_drafts`, and `store_analytics_events` (anonymous_id, ip_address, user_agent) to any `admin` with no tenant scope, while the sibling `store_quotes` and `business_os_snapshots` surfaces are gated on `allTenants`.
- Recommended improvement: gate on `resolveAdminTenantScope().allTenants`, or add `organization_id` + RLS to the intake tables and scope by it.

### Item: Response cache scope (new)

- Evidence: `apps/api/src/middleware/cache.ts:154-168`; `apps/api/src/routes/organizations.ts:153-182`; `apps/api/src/routes/dashboard.ts:16-50`; `apps/api/src/routes/business-os.ts:35-143,193-257`.
- What it does: keys authenticated responses by `:org=<req.orgId>`; the response body is computed from `resolveAdminTenantScope(req)` (which depends on the caller's memberships and super-admin flag), so two callers with the same active org but different scopes share an entry.
- Recommended improvement: include `allTenants`/sorted `orgIds` (or a scope hash) in the key; never let an org-keyed entry serve an all-tenants body; unit-test two membership sets with the same active org.

### Item: Background jobs (MT-P2-006)

- Evidence: `apps/worker/src/tasks/retention.ts:92-116`; `apps/worker/src/tasks/module-tasks.ts:992-1124,1287-1350`; `apps/api/src/lib/task-producer.ts:76-104`.
- What it does: service-role global report/purge jobs; per-row `organization_id` fan-out is correct; retention merges caller payload over defaults with a numeric sanity guard but no tenant guard.
- Missing controls: no payload tenant validation at the registry boundary; no user-facing enqueue path found (notify, webhook dispatcher, webhook retry only).
- Recommended improvement: validate org fields per task type; keep destructive tasks scheduled-only.
